records.name: Nicetown-Tioga Improvement Team
records.summary: Nicetown-Tioga Improvement Team is a neighborhood group, formed in 1998, that works as an umbrella for more than 50 local groups and block captains. Its monthly meeting is where neighbors hear about zoning and building plans and talk about housing, schools and jobs.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers. They also join free community events, such as school supply giveaways and movie nights.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the third Tuesday at 6 pm, September through June

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: via Zoom (online) and Zion Baptist Church (3601 N Broad St)

first_step.how: Join the monthly meeting on the third Tuesday at 6 pm on Zoom; the current link is on the group's meetings page.
first_step.basis: The membership page says everyone is welcome at meetings and the meetings page gives a fixed time, but neither speaks to newcomers directly.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings run on Zoom, and the agenda is posted on the meetings page once it is set, though some months list it as to be announced. The group reviews nearby zoning and development plans and hosts public meetings for some projects. Residents who come regularly can join committee talks or sign up to help with a program. The page does not say how long a meeting lasts or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Check the meetings page for the current Zoom link before the meeting, since the links on the site differ.
Camera use is optional on Zoom, and the page also lists a phone dial-in.
Expect the talk to center on zoning and building plans, the group's main work.

records.notes: Membership is for residents inside West Allegheny Avenue, Hunting Park Avenue, North 9th Street and North 16th Street, but anyone may attend meetings. No dues are stated. The two Zoom links on the site differ (the home page uses a 2026 link and the meetings page a 2025 one), so the record points to the meetings page instead of carrying a link. Cost is not stated. Phone and email are kept from the City list; the site does not show them.

records.name: Nueva Esperanza Housing and Economic Development
records.summary: Nueva Esperanza is a faith-based nonprofit in the Hunting Park area that runs charter schools, a college branch, job training, housing counseling, immigration legal help, and arts and music classes. It is also a City registered community organization for reviewing zoning and building plans in the North part of the city.
records.what_you_do: Use one of its programs, such as housing counseling, workforce training, immigration legal help, or arts and music classes, or attend its community events and outreach.

first_step.how: Call (215) 324-0746 or visit 4261 North 5th Street and ask which community meetings or programs fit you.
first_step.basis: The site lists programs and events and says to call or visit, but it does not say how to join the neighborhood meetings or volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a community meeting, volunteer shift, or class schedule, so ask at the office what is running. Its neighborhood work includes door to door outreach, daily street cleaning on the commercial corridor, tree planting, food outreach, and community fairs. The page does not say how long a first visit takes or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether the community meetings are open to residents or mainly to business owners.
The office is at 4261 North 5th Street, Philadelphia, PA 19140.

records.notes: Phone differs between the City list (215-324-2542) and the group's site and neighborhood page (215-324-0746). The group's own number is used. The site lists no meeting dates, volunteer steps or costs for community meetings, so the City registered civic role is not verified by the group's own pages. The homepage shows a September 15 item with no year; the year 2026 comes from the In the News page. Programs (charter schools, college, arts center, workforce) run under the same name and are not split into separate records.

records.name: RAH Civic Association
records.summary: RAH Civic Association is a City registered community organization in the North part of the city, made up of residents who share neighborhood news and follow zoning and development plans. Its own site says community meetings are on hold for now, and its newest dated post is from September 2024.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over when meetings are running. The group has also posted news about youth and community events, such as a book bag giveaway.

schedule.text: Community meetings start at 6:30 pm at St. James School when they resume; the site says they are on hold.

first_step.how: Email rcooper@rahcivic.org to ask whether a community meeting is scheduled and where, since the site says meetings are on hold.
first_step.basis: Meetings are on hold according to the site, and the only way in is an email to the contact, with a newsletter signup that may not work yet.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site says community meetings are on hold because of COVID-19 and will restart when it is safe. When they run, the page lists a 6:30 pm start at St. James School at 3217 W. Clearfield Street. The page does not give meeting days, how long meetings last, or any cost.
first_visit_tips: Confirm by email before you go, because the site does not show a current meeting.
The newest dated posts on the news page are from 2024, so ask whether the group is still meeting.

records.notes: Status changed from active to dormant. The newest dated items on the group's own news page are six posts all dated September 16, 2024, which may be one bulk import date. The City registry entry has no date of its own, so it does not count as dated evidence. Meetings are on hold with no restart date. The email signup form notes that it needs a storage option, so it may not work. The phone number is from the City list; the group's site does not show one.

records.name: Tioga United, Inc.
records.summary: Tioga United is a community organization in the Tioga area of North Philadelphia that serves as the neighborhood's Neighborhood Advisory Committee and links residents to City services. Its office helps neighbors with foreclosure, rent, benefits, and property questions, by appointment.
records.what_you_do: Call to set up an appointment at the office at 1539 W. Venango Street for help with foreclosure, rent, benefits, job training, small business start-up, blight, zoning, and property tax questions. You can also share what you like and want changed in the area.

schedule.text: Office open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, by appointment only; call ahead.

locations.label: Meeting place
locations.address: 1539 W. Venango St, Philadelphia PA 19140 and /or Virtual

first_step.how: Call (267) 639-6912 on a weekday between 9 am and 5 pm to book a visit at 1539 W. Venango Street.
first_step.basis: Any neighbor is invited to call or email for an appointment, which is a clear way in, but the site lists no regular meetings or volunteer steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The office is open by appointment only, so you call ahead on a weekday to set a time. Staff can help with foreclosure, rent, emergency housing information, benefits, job training, small business start-up, blight, and zoning questions. The page does not give a cost or say how long a visit takes.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since walk-in visits are not listed as welcome.
Ask whether the Zoom informational meetings have a date, because the site mentions them without a schedule or link.

records.notes: Status changed from active to dormant. The newest dated item on the group's press page is July 22, 2024, a citywide cleanup article rather than a Tioga event, and the copyright year does not count. The office still takes appointments on weekdays, and the events and newsletter pages are empty. Email conflict: the group's site shows Tiogaunited@hotmail.com while the City list shows info@tiogaunitednac.org; the site's address is used. Phone and contact name are from the City list and match the site phone.

records.name: Community on the Rise
records.summary: If you care about what gets built near you, Community on the Rise is a City registered community organization in the North Delaware part of the city that hears about zoning and development proposals.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and development plans in the area and meet to talk them over.
records.notes: Deep pass not completed: the group's website returned a certificate error on both the bare and www hostnames, so it is listed under blocked. The record is carried over from tier 1 without changes. The active status and the 2026-10 sign-of-life date come from the City registry, which has no date of its own, so treat them as unverified.

records.name: Community Schools @Hamilton Disston School
records.summary: Hamilton Disston is a school at 6801 Cottage Street that the City lists as a Community School, where partners run family supports, school events and after-school programs. Volunteer sign-up steps are not published on the school or City pages, so ask first.
records.what_you_do: Help with school based programs for students and families.

first_step.how: Email or call the Community School Coordinator, Undretta Williams, at undretta.williams@phila.gov or (267) 438-7945 to ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: Neither the school nor the City page says how volunteers sign up, so a newcomer has to make contact first.
first_step.what_to_expect: The City page does not describe a volunteer visit, so ask the coordinator what a first day looks like and what role is open. The listed activities include school events, resource fairs, family forums, parent cafes, and after-school programs. The coordinator's office hours are 8:30 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday.
first_visit_tips: Ask which clearances or background checks you must finish before a first visit.
Call during weekday office hours, 8:30 am to 5 pm.
The school is at 6801 Cottage St., Philadelphia, PA 19135.

records.notes: The volunteer portal listing returned HTTP 403, so volunteer steps, clearances and age rules are not known and are left out; the link is in blocked. The City program page now names Undretta Williams as coordinator with a different phone from the tier 1 contact (Madeline Cerulli, (215) 834-6277), so the City page is used; the tier 1 email was Madeline.Cerulli@phila.gov. Status is active because the school site posts 2026 to 2027 school year forms, but the site gives no month, so last_sign_of_life is left empty. The City page's posts are from 2023 and are older than those forms. Dropped lead: CORA Services, named only in a search snippet and not on the school or City pages.

records.name: Glen Foerd Conservation Corporation
records.summary: Glen Foerd is a historic riverfront estate at 5001 Grant Avenue, cared for by a nonprofit conservation corporation with Philadelphia Parks and Recreation. Neighbors can walk the free grounds, visit the mansion free on weekend afternoons, and join storytimes, workshops, yoga, tours and free open boating days.
records.what_you_do: Keep the estate open, run public tours, classes and events, and raise money for a mansion restoration.

schedule.text: Grounds open daily from 8 am to dusk. Mansion open free Fridays to Sundays, 10 am to 1 pm. Guided mansion tours on the second Saturday, 11 am to 12:30 pm.

cost.text: Grounds and mansion visits are free. Guided mansion tours on the second Saturday cost $10, and open boating days are free.

access.notes: A wheelchair lift reaches the front porch or first floor (the page is unclear which). A ramp leads to the sun porch. There is no elevator, and upper floors and restrooms are not wheelchair accessible. Grounds are mostly level, but riverside gravel paths are hard with mobility devices. Service animals are welcome.

first_step.how: Come to a free mansion visit on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday between 10 am and 1 pm, or book the second Saturday guided tour (11 am, $10) through the events page.
first_step.basis: The mansion is listed as free and open with no booking step, and events list dates and times, though tours are paid and several events have sold out.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is usually a self-guided walk: the grounds are a free public park, and the mansion is free on weekend afternoons. The second Saturday tour runs 11 am to 12:30 pm and costs $10, and you can register on the events page or pay at the door. The page says private events often close the estate to the public from 3 pm on many weekends from May through October.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page first, since private events can close the estate in the afternoon.
Park in the lot across from the community gardens or the lot behind the mansion, and follow the estate signs.
Wear shoes that handle gravel, since the riverside paths are hard with mobility devices.
Book popular tours early, since several events have sold out.

records.notes: Name and garden claim: the City garden listing (tier 1) describes a community garden with 20 raised beds at this address. The group's own pages describe an estate with a formal rose garden and a vineyard, and the visit page mentions community gardens across from the parking lot. No plot application, workday, or gardening sign-up appears on any page read, so the garden claim is kept only as an alias and an interest, and the name is changed to the operating nonprofit. A reviewer should confirm the garden contact before any garden listing. The site shows staff emails for group tours and planned gifts; they are not recorded, and the tier 1 email is kept. Dropped leads: EgoPo (theater company presenting one show run), Riverways (named on one listing), Art-Reach (a discount program), Not So Silent Cinema and Philly Fringe (performers and a festival), and Lily P.A.D.S. (named only in event titles).

notes: Batch of 7 groups. WebSearch used 1 of 1. WebFetch used 26 of 60 (failures included). Key findings: (1) Glen Foerd: tier 1 called this a community garden, but the group's own site describes an estate with events; name corrected, garden kept as alias and interest, confidence medium. (2) RAH Civic Association and Tioga United: the newest dated items on each group's own site are from 2024, so status changed from active to dormant. Both verdicts are left as publish; the owner may want dormant groups hidden. (3) The tier 1 sign-of-life dates for RCO-listed groups (2026-10) match the City registry fetch date, not a dated item. Status was changed only where the group's own dated pages were older. The importer may need a fix. (4) Contact conflicts resolved to the group's own site: Nueva Esperanza phone (215-324-0746 on site, 215-324-2542 on City list) and Tioga United email (Tiogaunited@hotmail.com on site, info@tiogaunitednac.org on City list). Hamilton Disston coordinator changed to Undretta Williams per the current City program page. (5) Dropped leads with reasons: Esperanza Arts Center (presented as one of Esperanza's programs), Esperanza Academy, Esperanza Cyber Charter and Esperanza College (schools covered under Esperanza), Hope Digital Skills (program with Eastern University), CORA Services (named only in a search snippet), Be-A-Gem Crossing (meeting venue), Cosacosa art at large (footer link to an unrelated art group), Opportunities Industrialization Center and Opportunities Tower (large workforce agencies named as past project partners), Kenderton School and Gratz High (schools), Williams Moore Reed Memorial Park (park). (6) Blocked: Community on the Rise (certificate error) and the Hamilton Disston volunteer portal (403). Four leads with no confirmed own website are in leads_only.
